summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease and a history of heart failure was admitted with acute shortness of breath after returning from church. He reported sudden onset of dyspnea, dry cough, leg swelling, and recent weight gain. In the ED, his oxygen saturation was in the mid-80s, requiring BiPAP support. Initial labs revealed severe hyperkalemia (K+ 8.2) and elevated BUN/creatinine, prompting emergent hemodialysis, which corrected his potassium and improved his respiratory status. He later developed chest pain with EKG changes and elevated troponins, consistent with a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. A nuclear stress test showed normal myocardial perfusion and preserved ejection fraction, so he was managed medically without intervention. His pulmonary edema improved with dialysis and supportive care. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor weight, continue home medications, and follow up with cardiology and nephrology.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Subendocardial infarction, initial episode of care
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of large intestine
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, benign, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
